chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him), after the Night of Hirr, when a man from among his companions stood up and said:
“You forbade us from arbitration, then ordered us to do it, so we do not know which of the two was more appropriate.” He (peace be upon him) struck one hand over the other and said:

key_terms.أَرْشَد: More appropriate or correct in guidance
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْهَرِيرِ: The Night of Hirr, referring to the night before the Battle of Siffin

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali initially forbid arbitration but then accept it after the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: This narration captures the pivotal moment after the Battle of Siffin (Night of Hirr) when a companion questioned Imam Ali (AS) regarding the apparent contradiction between his initial rejection of arbitration and his subsequent acceptance. The Imam’s gesture of clapping his hands signaled his readiness to elucidate the wisdom behind this strategic shift, highlighting the dynamic nature of his governance. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly view that Imam Ali’s decisions were guided by contextual necessity (siyasa) rather than rigid consistency, balancing principle with pragmatism to preserve the Muslim community.
